children: Hero Motors IPO was subscribed 1.18 times by 3.21 pm on the first day of bidding on Wednesday, with retail investors leading the subscription.

The retail portion was subscribed 1.96 times, while the non-institutional investors (NIIs) portion was subscribed 0.94 times. The qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) portion was subscribed 0.01 times.
The ₹1,000-crore IPO of Hero Motors will remain open for subscription till September 18. The company has fixed the price band at ₹79-84 per equity share.
The issue comprises a fresh issue of equity shares aggregating up to ₹600 crore and an offer-for-sale (OFS) of shares worth up to ₹400 crore by promoters.
Under the OFS, OP Munjal Holdings will divest shares worth ₹395 crore, while Hero Cycles Ltd will sell shares worth ₹5 crore.
Hero Motors garnered nearly ₹300 crore from anchor investors on Tuesday.
Of the fresh issue proceeds, ₹190 crore will be used to repay or prepay certain outstanding borrowings.
Another ₹200 crore will be used to purchase equipment required for capacity expansion at the company’s facility in Gautam Buddha Nagar, Uttar Pradesh.
The remaining proceeds will be used for inorganic growth through unidentified acquisitions and other strategic initiatives, as well as general corporate purposes.

Hero Motors is an automotive technology company engaged in designing, developing, manufacturing and supplying engineered powertrain solutions to automotive original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) in the US, Europe, India and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) region.
The company caters to global customers including BMW AG, Ducati Motor Holding S.P.A., Enviolo International Inc., Formula Motorsport Ltd and Hummingbird EV.
Hero Motors shares are expected to debut on the stock market on September 23.
